items.title: Allianz Profit Hits Record as Pimco Sees €32 Billion in Inflows
items.author: Stephan Kahl
items.content: <article>Allianz SE, the owner of bond manager Pacific Investment Management Co., generated record second-quarter profit on better results in its insurance and asset management businesses.</article>

items.title: India Bullion Exchange CEO Resigns in Blow to Fledgling Platform
items.author: Preeti Soni and Eddie Spence
items.content: <article>The head of India’s only dedicated bullion exchange has stepped down, dealing a setback to the four-year-old platform as it struggles to gain traction in one of the world’s largest gold markets.</article>

items.title: Adjoa Andoh Says ‘Bridgerton Was Lifechanging’
items.content: <article>In this conversation, actor Adjoa Andoh takes Mishal Husain behind the scenes of the hit show “Bridgerton,” and shares how she has shaped Lady Danbury’s character over the years. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: DeepSeek Restarts Funding for Ambitious AI Expansion | The China Show | 8/7/2026
items.content: <article>“Bloomberg: The China Show” is your definitive source for news and analysis on the world's second-biggest economy. From politics and policy to tech and trends, Yvonne Man and David Ingles give global investors unique insight, delivering in-depth discussions with the newsmakers who matter. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: South Africa Already Upgraded by Bond Market as Rating Firms Lag
items.author: Matthew Hill and Alexander Parker
items.content: <article>South African authorities are focused on hitting budget targets rather than pleasing credit-rating firms, according to the government’s top finance official — and the reward is a bond market that’s already pricing the country’s debt as investment grade.</article>

items.title: Goldman Skeptical of Dollar-Dominance Threats After Yen Support
items.author: Ruth Carson
items.content: <article>US support for Japan’s efforts to prop up the yen is unlikely to damage the dollar’s status as the most dominant reserve currency in the world, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.</article>

items.title: Zimbabwe’s VFEX Plans $5 Billion Market Value, Venture Board for Mining
items.author: Godfrey Marawanyika
items.content: <article>Zimbabwe’s dollar-denominated stock exchange plans to increase its market value by 25% over the next year as it rolls out new products, including a venture board to help junior mining and exploration companies raise capital.</article>

items.title: Iran Wants to Bar US, Israeli Ships From Hormuz in Deal
items.content: <article>Iran will seek to bar US and Israeli ships from the Strait of Hormuz and require compensation from hostile countries before they’re allowed to sail through it, according to local media reports on a proposed Iran-Oman deal. Bloomberg's Abeer Abu Omar has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Iran Strikes 'Hostile Targets'; Yen Weakens Past 158 | The Asia Trade 8/7/2026
items.content: <article>"Bloomberg: The Asia Trade" brings you everything you need to know to get ahead as the trading day begins in Asia. Bloomberg TV is live from Tokyo and Sydney with Shery Ahn and Haidi Stroud-Watts, getting insight and analysis from newsmakers and industry leaders on the biggest stories shaping global markets. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Asia Pacific Share Sales Overcome Volatility to Shatter Records
items.author: Julia Fioretti
items.content: <article>Blockbuster share sales from artificial intelligence-related companies in the Asia Pacific led to a record for equity capital markets activity last month, despite weakness in the region’s stock markets.</article>

items.title: UK IPO Slump Hurting Private Equity and Venture, PitchBook Says
items.author: Zainab Haji
items.content: <article>The UK’s sluggish market for initial public offering is leaving private equity and venture capital firms with fewer exit routes, increasing their reliance on sales to other buyout shops or large corporates for returns, PitchBook data show.</article>

items.title: Pacific Basin CEO Says Industry Faces Shift After Iran Conflict
items.content: <article>Martin Fruergaard, CEO of Pacific Basin, says the shipping firm is prepared for further business disruptions later this year, backed by a pipeline of 25 vessels and strategic flexibility. He speaks exclusively on "Bloomberg: The China Show." (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Hong Kong's Iconic Diners Go Global
items.content: <article>Hong Kong has exported everything from cinema to finance. Now, its iconic cha chaan teng diners are going global too. Mary Hui explains how these humble cafes have become a symbol of culture, migration and identity. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Copper Heads for Record Close in London on Tighter Global Market
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Copper headed for a record close in London after strong gains fueled by signs of tighter supply across the global market.</article>

items.title: Trading Strategies ‘Buried Alive’ by India’s Stock Auction
items.author: Savio Shetty and Samie Modak
items.content: <article>For much of the first week of trading under India’s new auction system to set closing stock prices, traders were convinced that one of the most consequential market structure reforms in years was faltering.</article>

items.title: Yen Surrenders Nearly Half Its Gains From US-Japan Intervention
items.author: Mia Glass
items.content: <article>The yen is heading into the end of the week having surrendered nearly half of its intervention-driven gains, fueling speculation among traders that authorities may step into the market again.</article>

items.title: Japan Confirms Three-Day Yen Intervention in Spring to Lift Yen
items.author: Erica Yokoyama
items.content: <article>Japan said it intervened in the currency market three times during the spring Golden Week holiday to prop up the yen, going beyond its recent twin-punch playbook with an additional round in an apparent effort to maximize the psychological impact on investors.</article>

items.title: Gold Set for Best Week Since January on Support From Dip-Buyers
items.author: Yihui Xie
items.content: <article>Gold was on track for its biggest gain in more than six months as dip-buyers supported prices above a key technical level while looking past flare-ups in the Strait of Hormuz that risked adding to energy-led inflation.</article>

items.title: Oil Gains on Iran, Bonds Drop Before US Jobs Data: Markets Wrap
items.author: Anand Krishnamoorthy
items.content: <article>Oil gained as prospects for a lasting agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remained elusive. Bonds fell on inflation concerns as traders awaited the US jobs report for clues on the path of interest rates.</article>

items.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 7
items.author: Nicholas Lua and Gabriel Levin
items.content: <article>Oil extended gains after a report that Iran attacked “hostile targets” in the Strait of Hormuz, with Tehran seeking to bar US ships from the critical waterway in a deal with Oman.</article>
